task.description: Space diving: find the maximum altitude from which a skydiver (total mass 190 kg, suit + parachute) can descend safely to the surface.

quota.note: Decrement once per code-edit + re-run cycle inside node_2b_modeling; at 0 with no convergence, trigger annealing rollback to hypothesis_layer.

hypothesis_layer.model_form: piecewise-aerodynamic-drag ODE, Mach-regime-dependent CD and cross-sectional area

atmosphere_source.name: hybrid: ambiance (0-80 km, ICAO 1993 std) + pymsis/MSIS (80-150 km, full numerical model)
atmosphere_source.access_method: Level 0 for both (locally installed Python packages, called in-process)
atmosphere_source.span_split_note: 0-80 km served by ambiance; 80-150 km served by pymsis. This is a deliberate multi-level/multi-source mix, recorded per data-source-routing.md's 'mixed-level' allowance.
atmosphere_source.fetched_at: recorded as a real Level 0 availability check, this run

ambiance_sample_artifact.description: Real sample values pulled from ambiance.Atmosphere during the Level 0 check

pymsis_sample_artifact.description: Real sample values pulled from pymsis.calculate (MSIS 2.0/2.1) at a fixed reference date/lon/lat
pymsis_sample_artifact.note: pymsis first call downloaded F10.7/Ap historical space-weather data from celestrak.org (a real external dependency, not a pure offline call like ambiance)

junction_continuity_check.description: Comparison of ambiance vs pymsis values at the 80 km handoff point
junction_continuity_check.interpretation: Not a bug: ICAO std atmosphere (idealized global mean) and MSIS (real, date/solar-cycle-dependent numerical model) legitimately differ at 80 km, where both models' uncertainty is large. This is a real, documented uncertainty in the combined 0-150 km profile, NOT a seamless junction. The ODE model step (Node 2b) must treat the 80 km handoff as a documented discontinuity/risk point, not a guaranteed-continuous boundary.

data_source_decision.rationale: Both chosen as Level 0 (local packages, no build step needed). ambiance confirmed for the 0-80 km range; pymsis confirmed for 80-150 km. The two do NOT join seamlessly at 80 km (ratio ~1.22 on density) — this is recorded as a real model uncertainty, not papered over.

availability_check.sample_artifact_id: inline samples above; hashes to be appended via audit_log.py when Node 2b consumes the combined array

data_source_decision.note: Only Node 1.5 writes this; downstream data-source fallbacks must surface as an anomaly, not by editing this in place. The 0-150 km combined profile is now sourced, but carries a documented, non-trivial junction uncertainty at 80 km that Node 2b must account for explicitly.

node2b_smoke_test_ambiance_39km.description: First real Node 2b run: descent from 39 km, ambiance density only, single-regime CD=1.0 (NO transonic/supersonic switching yet). Smoke test only, not the final answer.
node2b_smoke_test_ambiance_39km.caveat: This is a known intermediate result: because the piecewise CD=1/5/1.2 regime-switching logic is not yet implemented, the peak velocity is ~20% higher and the peak |a| much lower than the 2023 paper's fully-switched model (467.7 m/s, 9.68 m/s2). Do NOT treat these numbers as the verified final answer; they only confirm the ODE + data pipeline runs correctly end to end.

anomalies.description: ambiance and pymsis disagree by ~22% in density and ~5 K in temperature at the 80 km handoff point. This is a real model-form uncertainty, not a fetch error. Node 2b must treat the 80 km point as a documented discontinuity/risk point, not a guaranteed-continuous junction; recommend the ODE integration step flag sensitivity to this junction when reporting final results.
